Article Title: Amid opposition protest, Lok Sabha passes births & deaths bill
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha passed the Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Bill, 2026, without a debate and Rajya Sabha couldn’t transact any business Friday, amid sloganeering by opposition members over paper leaks, police crackdown of protesters and Ram temple “theft” issues.The bill was taken up for consideration and passage as soon as Lok Sabha reassembled after an hour-long adjournment at noon with BJP MP Dilip Saikia in the chair, leaving the opposition surprised as the house’s legislative business list showed it being listed against the name of home minister Amit Shah — who was not present — for moving it for passage.Several opposition members trooped into the well of the House, demanding Shah’s presence in LS, leading to the bill — seeking to amend provisions of the 1969 law to encourage timely registration of births and deaths — being passed by voice vote. Congress’s KC Venugopal and other MPs opposed its passage without debate.The bill proposed to make delayed registration of births and deaths stringent by requiring an order from a judicial magistrate (first class) for registrations after two years of the event.While Congress vehemently raised the issue of police crackdown on students, SP MPs were seen carrying placards of “chanda chor” to highlight the alleged temple donation theft.Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said it was unfortunate the opposition did not participate in the discussion, despite agreeing in the business advisory committee meeting.As proceedings began in RS, several opposition MPs demanded LoP Mallikarjun Kharge be allowed to speak, but chairperson C P Radhakrishnan ticked them off, saying they were still in “Emergency mode” and that they must also listen to others. As opposition members continued to raise slogans, agriculture minister Shivraj Chouhan accused them of indulging in “sadak-chhap (cheap)” politics and said, “They’re doing petty politics, playing with the dignity of the House. Democracy is being destroyed...”. RS was adjourned for the day around 11:20 pm.
Article Summary: Lok Sabha passed the Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Bill, 2026, without a debate. Rajya Sabha couldn't transact any business Friday, amid sloganeering by opposition members over paper leaks, police crackdown of protesters and Ram temple "theft" issues.

Article Title: CBI arrests 2 in Suvendu Adhikari aide murder case, probes political links
Article Text:
CBI arrests two in Chandranath Rath murder probe

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) on Friday arrested two brothers, Sagar Sonkar and Sahib Sonkar, in connection with the murder of Chandranath Rath, a close aide of West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari, in Kolkata. The arrests were made as part of the agency's probe into the alleged assassination plot, which investigators now believe may have links to a functionary of a rival political party.The two accused, who had worked with Rath, are expected to be produced before a special court in Kolkata later on Friday, officials said.Investigators alleged that Sagar Sonkar maintained regular contact with the office of a rival political party through landline calls while working with Rath. The agency is now examining those communications to identify the individual with whom he was allegedly in touch.According to officials, analysis of Sagar's call detail records revealed numerous calls made to the local office of the rival party. The CBI has also learnt that until 2020, Sagar had worked with an MLA of that party before later switching to the BJP.Officials said the agency had gathered sufficient material linking Sagar to the shooters allegedly hired to kill Rath.He is accused of arranging the contract and providing money for the execution of the murder.The CBI believes the conspiracy to eliminate Rath had been in motion since December 2025 and that the plan was repeatedly delayed before it was finally carried out.Rath, who served as Adhikari's personal assistant and was considered a key figure behind his election campaign in Kolkata's Bhabanipur ahead of the 2026 West Bengal Assembly elections, was shot dead on Jessore Road near Madhyamgram in North 24 Parganas district on May 6. He was travelling in a car when motorcycle-borne assailants opened fire.The killing took place two days after the declaration of results in the fiercely contested Bengal Assembly election, which saw the BJP defeat the Trinamool Congress and come to power in the state.The CBI has so far arrested six alleged shooters identified as Monu Singh, Raj Singh, Golu Singh, Mayank Raj Mishra, Vickey Maurya and Naveen Kumar Singh, along with middlemen Vinay Rai, Sanjay Rai and Vikas Mishra, who are alleged to have facilitated the contract. One accused remains absconding.The central agency took over the investigation from the West Bengal Police after a request from the state government. A seven-member special investigation team headed by a Deputy Inspector General from the CBI's Special Crime unit in Delhi has been constituted to investigate the case.
Article Summary: Sagar Sonkar and Sahib Sonkar arrested in connection with murder of Chandranath Rath. Rath was a close aide of West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari. The two accused are expected to be produced before a special court in Kolkata.

Article Title: SP pressures opposition to take up Ayodhya donation scam, Congress focuses on police crackdown
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party on Thursday forced Opposition bloc to take up the Ayodhya temple donation theft issue in Lok Sabha, even as Congress remained insistent on cornering Home Minister Amit Shah over the police crackdown on protesters.As a compromise, Opposition decided to take up both the issues simultaneously, evident in the loud protests both inside and outside Parliament.The competitive push has raised serious questions about the fate of Monsoon session, which has largely been washed out over the Jantar Mantar protests and the subsequent police action on students.Well-placed sources said the anti-BJP bloc will not concede unless their demands are heeded. A senior Congress manager told TOI that a washout of the remaining ten days of Parliament session seems a strong possibility.Sources said Samajwadi Party along with allies has decided to push for an “adjournment motion” to discuss Ayodhya temple theft, as against a short-duration discussion.The implications of accepting the “adjournment motion” are grave, given that it conveys a censure of govt, besides the possibility of House adopting a resolution on the subject at the conclusion of the debate.Ruling BJP is unlikely to yield to Opposition on Ayodhya scam, or on the demand regarding the home minister.“It is a matter of ten days now. The govt may just play it out instead of courting embarrassment,” a senior Congress functionary said.In the meeting of the allies on Thursday, sources said, SP leaders strongly demanded that Opposition take up the temple theft issue in the House. Congress managers argued that “chanda chori” was important, but the issue of Amit Shah could not be left midway. So, Opposition decided to take up both issues this week.Ahead of the proceedings on Thursday, Opposition mounted a loud protest over the twin issues. Members, including Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, KC Venugopal, Dharmendra Yadav, Mahua Moitra, Thol Thirumavalavan, NK Premachandran, Sanjay Raut and Mahua Maji, held a large banner with the question, “Who gave the order?” – a reference to the person who authorised the firing of pellet guns on protesting students. In front of the MPs were placed donation boxes (daan paatra), with members putting money in them – an allusion to the temple theft.The scene was repeated inside the lower house where SP members raised slogans of “chanda chor, gaddi chhor”, joined in by others, with Congress and allies also raising the heat on the police crackdown and demanding that Shah come to House.
Article Summary: Samajwadi Party forced Opposition bloc to take up the Ayodhya temple donation theft issue in Lok Sabha. Congress remained insistent on cornering Home Minister Amit Shah over the police crackdown on protesters. As a compromise, Opposition decided to taking up both the issues simultaneously.

Article Title: BJP trying to force Muslims, minorities to worship Hindu deities, says Owaisi; DMK slams Vande Mataram bill as 'fraud'
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: AIMIM leader Asaduddin Owaisi Thursday slammed the bill making “insult” to Vande Mataram a crime, saying BJP is trying to force Muslims and minorities to worship Hindu deities, while DMK claimed it was hurting the secular fabric of the country.DMK MP A Raja, who moved an amendment to the bill in Lok Sabha, called the legislation a “fraud” perpetrated by Modi govt on people. He said Constituent Assembly approved only two paragraphs of the song. “The Constitution came from Constituent Assembly, and it is unconstitutional to exceed Constituent Assembly. This bill will not stand judicial scrutiny. This is against the secular fabric of India and we will not accept it,” he said.Meanwhile, as Congress attacked govt for passing the bill amid din, MP KC Venugopal questioned the absence of home minister Amit Shah from LS when his ministry’s legislation to “prevent the insult to national symbols” was taken up. Manickam Tagore too criticised Shah’s absence from the House. Some members of Congress — which has been asking Shah questions about the police crackdown on student protesters — termed the bill as “divisive” and against secularism.Owaisi argued “national anthem — Jana Gana Mana” is a reflection of the country and its people, but Vande Mataram is about prayers to “devi-devta”. “This bill is a grave violation of Article 25 that gives freedom of religion. This is intended to convert India into a Hindu theocratic state.”Congress MP Tariq Anwar said govt should have taken opposition parties into confidence for this bill but “this govt tries to impose its views on people”.He said Vande Mataram was a principal song of the freedom struggle, and all Congress functions start with the national song. “But controversy is about govt interfering with the decision of Constituent Assembly...objectionable words were removed because India is secular.” Party MP Ujjwal Raman Singh called the bill’s passage without discussion a “black day” in India’s history.
Article Summary: AIMIM leader Asaduddin Owaisi slammed the bill making “insult’ to Vande Mataram a crime. DMK MP A Raja called the legislation a “fraud” perpetrated by Modi govt on people.

Article Title: 'First you broke their bones, now filing FIRs': Rahul Gandhi warns PM Modi, Amit Shah to not 'threaten Gen Z into silence'
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi took a jab at PM Modi and Amit Shah, calling them 'India's past'

NEW DELHI: Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Friday targeted Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah over the action against student protesters, alleging that the government was trying to "silence Gen Z" through FIRs and social media takedowns after directly attacking them during protests.Making a statement on X, the Congress leader said, "PM Modi and Amit Shah - you cannot threaten Gen Z into silence. First you broke their bones. Now you are filing FIRs and taking down their accounts."Further taking a jab at PM Modi and Shah, he added, "You are India’s past. Be careful about how you treat India’s future."This comes a day after Rahul demanded a Supreme Court-monitored, high-powered committee to investigate the alleged police action against student protesters during the July 20 demonstration at Delhi's Jantar Mantar.In a post on X, the Congress MP had called for an impartial probe into the alleged use of force, saying, "Students deserve justice. An independent SC-monitored high-powered committee must be constituted to probe brutalities against our students."Gandhi also shared a video purportedly showing police action against the protesters. The footage appeared to show police personnel lathi-charging demonstrators, while another clip showed a man in civilian clothes forcefully pushing a student carrying the Indian flag onto the road.His demand came as Opposition MPs from several INDIA bloc parties staged a protest at Makar Dwar in the Parliament complex over the alleged police action against students and the alleged embezzlement of donations meant for the Ram Temple in Ayodhya.The MPs gathered around 10.30 am, carrying placards questioning who ordered the police action at Jantar Mantar and raising slogans demanding accountability from the Centre over the alleged use of force and the alleged financial irregularities in donations to the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Temple.The protest took place hours before the Rajya Sabha was scheduled to consider and pass the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi accuses PM Modi and Amit Shah of trying to "silence Gen Z" through FIRs and social media takedowns after directly attacking them during protests. This comes a day after Rahul demanded a Supreme Court-monitored, high-powered committee to investigate the alleged police action.

Article Title: Parts of Manusmriti now part of 'curriculum', says Mallikarjun Kharge
Article Text:
Rajya Sabha LoP Mallikarjun Kharge speaks in Rajya Sabha during the Monsoon Session of Parliament, in New Delhi

NEW DELHI: The debate on Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill in RS Thursday turned into a heated argument between treasury benches and opposition when leader of the opposition Mallikarjun Kharge read out what he claimed Hindi translation of a portion from Manusmriti.Kharge alleged portions of Manusmriti have become part of the "curriculum" under BJP govt. He was challenged by leader of the House J P Nadda, who asked the LoP to produce the "original manuscript" for authentication.RS chairperson CP Radhakrishnan asked Kharge what Manusmriti had to do with the bill. Kharge claimed, "Manusmriti teaches that if a 'Shudra' listens to Veda, his ears should be filled with shards; if he reads Ved aloud, his tongue should be cut off; and if he retains its words, his body should be dismembered."BJP MP Sudhanshu Trivedi slammed Kharge citing B R Ambedkar's writings to argue there was no untouchability in the era of Manu.
Article Summary: Opposition leader of the opposition Mallikarjun Kharge read out what he claimed Hindi translation of a portion from Manusmriti. He was challenged by leader of House J P Nadda, who asked the LoP to produce the "original manuscript" for authentication.

Article Title: NEET leak row: Opposition politicising issue, government has brought in strict law, says BJP
Article Text:
BJP MP Sudhanshu Trivedi speaks in the Rajya Sabha during the Monsoon session of Parliament, in New Delhi

NEW DELHI: Treasury bench MPs condemned opposition for politicising the NEET-UG paper leak issue and recent protests, as they highlighted how govt has taken steps in the right direction to address concerns by holding dialogue with students to end their agitation and proposing a stronger law against exam paper leaks.Participating in the discussion, BJP MP Sudhanshu Trivedi listed government's efforts to resolve student protest and also highlighted how senior ministers J P Nadda and Jitendra Singh held talks with them and activist Sonam Wangchuk, who was fasting for 26 days.Government agreed to the demands of students, he said, adding Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as education minister, a fast-track court was set up and a task force was set up by PM Narendra Modi under Aadhaar architect Nandan Nilekani.On Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, Trivedi said there are three basic principles - a sensitive approach towards students, a secured process and a stringent law against paper leaks. Trivedi said the bill provides for stringent punishment, time-bound investigation and speedier justice. These will prove key in preventing paper leaks, he said.Targeting opposition MPs, who raised questions on PM Modi's educational qualifications, he said those who have never themselves faced competition in exams, in education, or in their own political parties are now teaching the govt. "In contrast, our politicians and our PM have faced competition and exams and have risen from the ground," Trivedi said.JDU's Sanjay Jha supported the bill, saying this should not be looked at from political prospects.Shiv Sena's Milind Deora suggested students should be involved in the reform process by giving them a formal role in the consultations.
Article Summary: Treasury bench MPs condemned opposition for politicising the NEET-UG paper leak issue and recent protests. They highlighted how govt has taken steps in the right direction to address concerns. BJP MP Sudhanshu Trivedi listed government's efforts to resolve student protest.

Article Title: 'Abusing not a crime': CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke slams FIR against Noida woman, recalls UP CM video
Article Text:
CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke (Image Credit: X)





NEW DELHI: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke has questioned the registration of an FIR against a woman accused of using abusive language against Prime Minister Narendra Modi , asking whether there were "two laws" in the country and why similar action was not taken against BJP leaders and IT cell members accused of using objectionable language.In a video shared by the outfit on X on Friday, Dipke said he had learnt that a case had been registered against a woman for using abusive language and questioned why similar action had not been taken in other cases.Also read: Noida woman apologises over PM Modi 'abuse' video, claims she was 'influenced' “If you are registering cases for abusing, when will cases be registered against those BJP IT cell people who have been using abusive language for women online for years?” Dipke asked.He alleged that several such social media users had repeatedly used objectionable language against women while openly identifying themselves with the BJP.“They have been using all kinds of words, not respecting women from any angle. And they proudly wrote in their bio, ‘Followed by PM Modi’. Such people have abused girls. When will the case be filed on them?” he added.Dipke also referred to remarks made by BJP leaders in the past, questioning why similar action had not been taken against them.“It is not just the BJP's IT cell. Their Member of Parliament, Ramesh Bidhuri ji, what words did he use for a fellow Member of Parliament, everyone remembers that,” he said.He also cited Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath, alleging that a video had surfaced in which he used abusive language against a camera person.“The CM of UP even had a video, where he had abused a camera person. So, what is going on? Are there two laws in this country? There is a separate law for youth and a separate law for BJP and their leaders,” he said.Claiming that abusive language was not a criminal offence, Dipke said cases should not be filed merely over such remarks.“Abusing is not a crime. It is a bad thing, explain it to the person that they should not use such language, but why is a case being filed? If cases are to be filed for abusing, highest number of cases will be filed against the BJP's IT cell, because they are the ones who have abused women the most. And it will be against BJP's leaders, who have used bad language for years, even inside the Parliament,” he said.In a post accompanying the video, CJP said: “Will an FIR be filed against all those IT Cell members who have been abusing women for the last several years?”The remarks came a day after a Zero FIR was registered at the Expressway police station in Noida against Ruchika Singh for allegedly using abusive and objectionable language against Prime Minister Narendra Modi during a protest at Jantar Mantar on July 23.The FIR was lodged on the complaint of Ghaziabad resident Smriti Singh under Sections 352 (intentional insult to provoke breach of peace), 353(1) (statements conducing to public mischief) and 356(1) (defamation) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.Police said the Zero FIR would be transferred to New Delhi for further investigation.
Article Summary: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke questions the registration of an FIR against a woman accused of using abusive language against Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Dipke asks whether there were "two laws" in the country and why similar action was not taken against BJP leaders and IT cell members. The remarks came a day after a Zero FIR was registered against Ruchika Singh.

Article Title: Reveal names of people who gave offer to join BJP, Maharashtra minister asks CJP's Abhijeet Dipke
Article Text:
Radhakrishna Vikhe Patil challenged Abhijeet Dipke to name BJP members who offered him party membership.





PUNE: State cabinet minister and senior BJP member Radhakrishna Vikhe Patil on Friday challenged Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke to reveal the name of the person who offered him to join BJP and threatened him.After returning to his hometown Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar following the CJP protest in Delhi, Dipke claimed during a media interaction that he and his family members received threats after he refused the offer of joining BJP.Reacting to Dipke’s statement, Vikhe Patil said, “Instead of making ambiguous statements, Dipke should speak clearly and reveal the names of people who offered him to join our party and threatened him. He has led a successful agitation and the govt accepted the protesters’ demands. He should avoid making political statements.”Vikhe Patil also accused political parties of trying to take political mileage out of the CJP protest against the central govt. “Opposition parties are trying to find an opportunity to target the govt after the CJP protest and Dipke should not fall prey to the opposition’s trap,” he added.
Article Summary: Radhakrishna Vikhe Patil challenged Abhijeet Dipke to name BJP members who offered him party membership. Dipke claimed during a media interaction that he and his family members received threats after he refused the offer of joining BJP. The state cabinet minister also accused political parties of trying to take political mileage out of the CJP protest.

Article Title: Complaint filed against MP Pappu Yadav over Parliament protest on Ram Mandir donation 'theft' row
Article Text:
Complaint filed against Purnia MP Pappu Yadav in Delhi over Parliament protest





NEW DELHI: A complaint has been filed against Independent Purnia MP Rajesh Ranjan alias Pappu Yadav at Delhi's Jehangirpuri Police Station over his protest inside the Parliament complex on the alleged Ram Mandir donation embezzlement issue, as reported by news agency ANI.The complaint, lodged by Surya Maithil, accuses Yadav of hurting religious sentiments during the demonstration. Maithil also alleged that several INDIA bloc MPs backed the protest.Claiming that Yadav insulted religious symbols, Maithil said, "The way Pappu Yadav insulted the saffron today and staged the drama outside Parliament, supported by Rahul Gandhi, Dimple Yadav, Awadhesh Kumar and other INDIA alliance MPs, has hurt the sentiments of Sanatanis. During the protest, he even placed a picture of Lord Ram Lalla Virajman under his feet."He said he had sought immediate legal action against Yadav and others, urging Union home minister Amit Shah , the Delhi Police commissioner and other senior police officials to act on the complaint.On Thursday, the Parliament complex witnessed an unusual opposition protest in the form of a street play over the alleged Ram Mandir donation "theft" row.Opposition MPs also demanded that Amit Shah address Parliament over the recent police action against protesting students.Amid slogans of "Chanda chor, gaddi chhod", "Jawab tumko dena hoga" and "Amit Shah, sadan mein aao", Pappu Yadav, dressed as a temple priest in saffron robes, carried a photograph of Lord Ram and enacted a symbolic performance. As fellow opposition MPs, playing devotees, dropped donations into a collection box, Yadav was shown pocketing the money instead, before another MP confronted him in the staged act.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Complaint filed against Purnia MP Pappu Yadav in Delhi over Parliament protest. Yadav dressed as a temple priest in saffron robes and enacted a symbolic performance. As fellow opposition MPs dropped donations into a collection box, Yadav was shown pocketing the money.

Article Title: Forest officer held for accepting Rs 5 lakh in bribe
Article Text: Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar: The anti-corruption bureau (ACB) on Friday arrested a divisional forest officer from Beed for allegedly accepting Rs 5 lakh as part of a Rs 45 lakh bribe demand in exchange for releasing plantation funds and extending official favours to a subordinate officer.Police identified the accused as Srinivas Linganna Lakhmawad (40), divisional forest officer, social forestry division, Beed. The complaint was lodged on Thursday by a forest range officer.Superintendent of police Madhuri Kedar Kangane said, “The accused demanded Rs 45 lakh from a forest range officer for facilitating the release of plantation funds, refraining from pursuing a suspension proposal against him, securing two pending annual salary increments and halting an inquiry into nursery-related works. After verification of the complaint, a trap was laid and he was caught while accepting Rs 5 lakh in cash. ”Additional SP Shashikant Shingare said the trap was executed on Friday by a team led by inspector Bhaskar Navale of the Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar ACB unit at Lakhmawad’s residence in Urja Heights on Canal Road near Nagar Naka in Beed.The police said the accused attended the DPDC meeting during the day and reached home after the meeting for receiving the bribe amount from his subordinate. A case has been registered against the accused under Section 7 of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.
Article Summary: Police identified the accused as Srinivas Linganna Lakhmawad (40), divisional forest officer, social forestry division, Beed. The complaint was lodged on Thursday by a forest range officer. A trap was laid and he was caught while accepting Rs 5 lakh in cash.

Article Title: Re-NEET row: Bombay high court finds no discrepancy in answer sheets, dismisses 2 petitions; imposes Rs 5,000 fine
Article Text:
The Bombay High Court dismissed four petitions challenging the re-NEET examination results

(With ANI inputs)





Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar: The Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar bench of the Bombay high court has dismissed two petitions challenging the re-NEET examination results after examining the original answer sheets and finding no discrepancies in the evaluation.The court also imposed a fine of Rs 5,000 on each petitioner for approaching it with what it termed incorrect and unverified claims.The petitions had alleged that the National Testing Agency NTA ) declared incorrect results and made errors while evaluating the answer sheets.The matter was heard by a division bench of Justice N. B. Suryawanshi and Justice A. D. Shinde.Taking note of the seriousness of the allegations, the bench directed that the original answer sheets of the concerned students be brought from Delhi in sealed envelopes.The court examined the answer sheets and also allowed the students, their parents and their lawyers to inspect the original records.After scrutinising the material, the court found that the marks awarded by the NTA and the declared results matched the original answer sheets, with no errors or discrepancies in the evaluation.Senior panel advocate Rohit Sarvagya, appearing for the Centre and the NTA, produced all the original documents before the court during the hearing.After considering the submissions and examining the original records, the bench dismissed two petitions and imposed a cost of Rs 5,000 on each petitioner for filing the pleas based on incorrect and unverified information.With the high court's ruling, the re-NEET examination results declared by the NTA have received judicial confirmation.
Article Summary: The Bombay High Court dismissed four petitions challenging the re-NEET examination results. The court also imposed a fine of Rs 5,000 on each petitioner for approaching it with what it termed incorrect and unverified claims. The petitions had alleged that the National Testing Agency NTA ) declared incorrect results and made errors while evaluating the answer sheets.

Article Title: Congress stages rasta roko in Kalyan over police action on Jantar Mantar protesters
Article Text:
Congress workers staged a protest in Kalyan West against alleged police action.





KALYAN: Congress workers staged a rasta roko protest at Shivaji Chowk in Kalyan West to protest against the alleged police action on students demonstrating at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi over the alleged paper leak issue.Led by Navin Singh, Kalyan District President, the protesters raised slogans against the Centre and demanded action over the alleged assault on students and peaceful demonstrators by the Delhi Police.Traffic was briefly affected in the area before police intervened.The party also submitted a memorandum to the Kalyan tehsildar, addressed to the President of India, seeking an inquiry into the alleged police action against students and Congress leaders, including Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and other party leaders, during the protest at Delhi.In the memorandum, the Congress demanded the immediate resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, holding him morally responsible for the alleged irregularities in the paper leak. The party also sought an urgent discussion in Parliament on alleged examination irregularities and issues affecting students' future.The memorandum further demanded that all FIRs and criminal cases registered against students and peaceful protesters be withdrawn immediately.Among those present at the protest were corporator Samina Sheikh, former corporator Iftekar Khan and other Congress office-bearers and workers. Police maintained security at the protest site and ensured traffic movement was restored after the demonstration concluded.
Article Summary: Congress workers staged a rasta roko protest at Shivaji Chowk in Kalyan West. They were protesting against the alleged police action on students demonstrating at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi. The protesters raised slogans against the Centre and demanded action over the alleged assault on students and peaceful demonstrators.

Article Title: DMK slams TVK govt for `renaming’ Thayumanavar welfare scheme
Article Text: Chennai: Former minister S S Sivasankar and DMK organisational secretary R S Bharathi on Friday alleged that the TVK govt has renamed the Thayumanavar scheme launched by former chief minister M K Stalin to deliver ration commodities at the doorsteps of senior citizens and persons with disabilities.Addressing reporters at Anna Arivalayam, Bharathi said the Nilgiris district administration had issued a statement where the term `Thayumanavar’ was dropped while mentioning about the scheme. Bharathi alleged that the TVK govt was renaming existing scheme due to its inability to launch new schemes or fulfill its electoral promises. He added that the ruling party was attempting to erase M K Stalin’s legacy from public memory, but would fail.Sivasankar said the TVK administration felt threatened by the popularity of DMK-era initiatives such as the CM Breakfast Scheme, Vidiyal Payanam, and Naan Mudhalvan. He said that removing ‘Thayumanavar’ from the doorstep ration scheme was part of a systemic effort to rename DMK initiatives. ``Such attempts to undermine the previous government’s achievements would backfire,’’ he said.
Article Summary: Former minister S S Sivasankar and DMK organisational secretary R S Bharathi on Friday alleged that the TVK govt has renamed the Thayumanavar scheme. The scheme was launched by former chief minister M K Stalin to deliver ration commodities at the doorsteps.

Article Title: Truck driver dies in road accident near Salem
Article Text: SALEM: A driver died in an accident involving a truck, a pickup van and a bus near Mecheri in Salem district on Wednesday. More than 10 bus passengers suffered injuries in the accident.According to the Mecheri police, a TNSTC bus carrying 51 passengers was heading to Karur from Mettur when a speeding pickup van attempted to overtake it. “The pickup van collided head-on with a truck coming from the opposite direction,” said an officer at the Mecheri police station. The truck grazed the bus, shattering its windows and injuring more than 10 passengers seated near the windows.Truck driver C Penumoola Revanthra, 53 of Guntur in Andhra Pradesh died on the spot. The injured were rushed to govt hospitals in Mettur and Omalur.Fire service personnel, assisted by Mecheri police and residents, worked to move the damaged truck and pickup van to the roadside. Traffic on the Mettur–Salem highway was disrupted for an hour.The Mecheri police registered a case.
Article Summary: More than 10 bus passengers suffered injuries in the accident. Truck driver C Penumoola Revanthra, 53 of Guntur in Andhra Pradesh died on the spot. Traffic on the Mettur–Salem highway was disrupted for an hour.

Article Title: Three acquitted in 1992 murder of abkari contractor in Palakkad
Article Text:
Kochi

:





A CBI special court in Kochi on Friday acquitted three accused in the 1992 murder of abkari contractor K G Munna.The acquitted are P Vijayan, P K Sudheer and George Mangalam, all natives of Kottapuram in Palakkad. CBI court Judge P K Mohandas pronounced the verdict.Vijayan and Sudheer were abkari contractors while Mangalam was an employee of Vijayan. According to the prosecution, Vijayan and Sudheer promised to pay Munna Rs 1.5 lakh if he refrained from bidding at an auction held in 1992 for running arrack and brandy shops. As promised, Sudheer paid Munna Rs 1.5 lakh but conspired to recover the amount. The prosecution alleged that the accused assaulted Munna with a jack lever in his car in Palakkad.The case was initially registered by Sreekrishnapuram Police before being transferred to the crime branch and then to CBI.Acquitting the accused, the court observed that the prosecution did not produce any evidence to establish the alleged criminal conspiracy and its case rested entirely on circumstantial evidence.
Article Summary: P Vijayan, P K Sudheer and George Mangalam are acquitted. The prosecution alleged that the accused assaulted Munna with a jack lever in his car. The case was initially registered by Sreekrishnapuram Police before being transferred to crime branch and then to CBI.

Article Title: Plea in Kerala HC seeks to invalidate election of Thiruvananthapuram mayor & deputy mayor
Article Text:
Kochi:





An appeal has been filed before the high court by S P Deepak, a CPM leader and councillor of the Thiruvananthapuram corporation, seeking to invalidate the election of the mayor and deputy mayor on the ground that 20 BJP councillors participated in the election after taking an oath in violation of the Kerala Municipality Act.A bench of Justices K Natarajan and Johnson John issued notices to the State Election Commission and the 20 councillors on the appeal. Earlier, in a petition filed by Deepak, a single bench had declared invalid the oath administered to the 20 councillors and directed them to retake the oath in accordance with the Act. The court had found that the councillors had taken the oath in the names of various deities, while some had taken the oath in the name of party martyrs.Deepak had contended that the Third Schedule to the Kerala Municipality Act permits the oath to be taken only in the name of God or by making a solemn affirmation. However, the single bench had clarified that the election of the councillors could not be set aside merely because of the illegality in the oath-taking ceremony, as they had been duly elected by the electorate through a democratic process.In the appeal, Deepak contended that since the oath taken by the 20 councillors had been declared invalid, they could not be said to have legally assumed office when they participated in the election of the mayor and deputy mayor. Consequently, the votes cast by them were void and the election of the mayor and deputy mayor, which was founded on those votes, was liable to be declared illegal and set aside.
Article Summary: A bench of Justices K Natarajan and Johnson John issued notices to the State Election Commission and the 20 councillors on the appeal. Earlier, in a petition filed by Deepak, a single bench had declared invalid the oath taken by the councillors.
